title: bee-swarming wiring: the herding execution path and its orchestrator bookkeeping
action: Per D4 (second half) and D1: add a short section to swarming-reference.md — when the user asks for a cell to run through an external agent, the orchestrator dispatches it with bee herding run (background Bash, one completion notification), reads result-N.json's validated JSON, then does ALL bee bookkeeping itself: verify per the cell's proof type, bee cells finish with the worker's evidence, reservations, judge. The pane worker never runs bee verbs. Name the boundary: herding execution is user-requested per cell in scope A — never the default dispatch path (that is scope B, trigger-gated). Include the --continue round loop for blocked results.

truths: swarming-reference.md names the orchestrator as the only bee-verb actor on a herding-run cell
Scope A boundary stated: herding dispatch is user-requested, never the default

report.outcome: swarming-reference.md documents the bee herding run execution path: pane worker stays bee-ignorant, orchestrator owns all bee bookkeeping, scope A is user-requested per cell never the default
report.tests: rg -n "bee-ignorant (D4)" plus fence/heading structure check — green — docs-only wave-barrier cell: both must_haves truths verified present in the added section; release-manifest --check is expected to mismatch on this file until the orchestrator's wave-close regen (regen_obligation_ack: wave-barrier, obligation.rs L218); pointer_integrity's one failure is pre-existing and unrelated (confirmed red on the base commit via git stash, in gates-and-delegation.md which this cell never touches)
